items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: Sonny Stitt took me under his wings maybe about that time or whatever, and I used to hang with Sonny, and I’d try to pick Sonny’s brain.

ctx.x: I’m trying to imagine your thinking about yourself when you were doing those two years with George Benson. Were you happy with your playing?

No. I’d go home and cry every night, you understand? Because George displays all the, George is just — and I was trying to play as many notes as he was and trying to be as technically proficient. And George is one of the greatest players. You know Jimmy Smith, I hung out with Phineas Newborn Jr. I’ve been around giants you understand? So I know the difference between a giant and a regular player. I got to, say for instance Sonny Stitt took me under his wings maybe about that time or whatever, and I used to hang…

Sonny Stitt thought I was pretty good you know. Years and years and years later I was living in Memphis, Tennessee and Sonny comes through Memphis and he would travel and play with local rhythm sections and so — but I hadn’t seen Sonny in a long time. And by this time I’ve got a foot of hair and platform shoes and a full beard. And so I go back to the dressing room after the gig to see Sonny Stitt you see. And Sonny Stitt had just come out of being in a coma for 13 days. 13 days he was in a coma. But the thing is…
